name: worktree-write-scope-decisions
body:
Worktree-only write scope for code-writer agents deepens `requirements.constraint.code-writer-scope-worktree-only`. Model: every generated code-writer agent's `edit` grants target the worktree mirror `apg/.worktrees/*/` rather than a repo-root path. opencode resolves path-scoped globs against the session workspace root (the main checkout), so the worktree form reaches the worktree, and a root grant makes main writable. fs scope resolution: `ts.apg-opencode-suite.lib.apg.fsScopeDecision` resolves a candidate against the caller directory, and `ts.apg-opencode-suite.lib.apg.agentFsGlobs` supplies the effective `edit`-action scope (allow and deny, last match wins, read from the agent's opencode 2.x `permissions` array), so the fs tools read allow and deny rules, ordered, rather than allow globs alone. Scope is decided in one frame: the candidate path resolves to an absolute path against the session workspace root (the main-checkout root opencode uses) and matches grants anchored at that root, so an absolute path outside `
/apg/.worktrees/

/` is refused. The way a tool learns the acting agent's identity under opencode 2.x is an explicit accepted open item verified by unit/int tests against a faked V2 tool context (`requirements.constraint.agent-fs-per-path-permission`): opencode 2.x documents zero acting-agent identity on a tool executor and a custom plugin tool's permission action is its own tool name. An unresolvable acting agent refuses every path. Release-agent: releases run from MAIN, so the release-agent's write grants target the main checkout; it is one of the two agent carve-outs of `global.constraint.worktree-isolation` and carries zero worktree mirror. Its main-write set is repo-specific: the agent-builder analyses the repo (version files, packaging formulae, changelog, release scripts) and recommends the set, confirmed through the coordinator interview like build gates and test tiers; the spec fixes the policy alone.
